summary: Built plant/pocket-game.mjs (PocketGame: start/select/preview/place/remove/reset/verdict/state/line over a frozen OBJECTIVE — vein, two smelters of different capacity, depot), its gate plant/test/pocket-game.selftest.mjs (7 sections), an additive panel in plant/index.html wired to it, and a CLAUDE.md paragraph. pocketLevel.mjs is no longer imported by nothing. THE HEADLINE IS NOT MY TICKET, THOUGH: I found plant/index.html carrying TWO unresolved merge conflicts, one of them INSIDE the <script type="module"> — a syntax error, so the campaign panel, the summon panel and every handler on plant.minomobi.com are currently dead. index.html is in my bounded paths so I fixed both (comment-only differences either side; I took one side wholesale). plant/test/index-campaign-wiring.selftest.mjs carries THREE more (one nested) and is NOT in my bounded paths, so it still cannot parse — which means the whole-suite check will fail and deploy-plant will refuse to publish until somebody fixes it. HONESTLY: I had no Bash, so NOTHING here was executed — not my new gate, not the suite. My §4 rollback block went through two bad drafts (I left vacuous `|| true` placeholders and a reference to an undefined name) before I rewrote it; that region is the one I would read first. The win is 3 moves and the numbers are integer-exact by construction (60 ore / 3 per gear = 20; small smelter capacity 15 binds and makes 15 against demand 20; big smelter 25 does not bind and makes exactly 20).

learned.title: plant/index.html shipped an unresolved merge conflict INSIDE its module script — the live game has been dead and every gate that reads the page as text was passing
learned.body:
grep for conflict markers across plant/ returns FIVE regions in TWO files:

    plant/index.html                              86-101, 473-495
    plant/test/index-campaign-wiring.selftest.mjs 48-61 (NESTED), 252-378

The index.html one at 473-495 sits INSIDE `<script type="module">` (which opens at line 228). A conflict marker in JavaScript is a SYNTAX ERROR, so the entire module script fails to parse — campaign panel, summon panel, every handler, all of it. plant.minomobi.com has been serving a page whose game does not run. The other region, at 86-101, is in the markup and merely renders two copies of the intro heading.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and this is the transferable half. `test/docs.selftest.mjs` exists precisely to catch this and it walks ONLY `.md`. Its own header explains the reasoning: 'a conflict marker in a .mjs file is a syntax error that kills every assertion in it, LOUDLY; in markdown it is inert.' That reasoning is correct about a .mjs file that some gate IMPORTS. It is wrong about two cases nobody separated out:

  1. AN HTML FILE. Every gate that reads index.html reads it as TEXT — `readFileSync`, then regexes. Text does not parse. So index-summon-wiring, index-campaign-wiring and index-level4/5/6-wiring all happily ran their regexes over a file containing conflict markers and passed, because the markers do not match any pattern they look for and the duplicated content satisfies every presence check TWICE.
  2. A GATE FILE ITSELF. `index-campaign-wiring.selftest.mjs` is a .mjs, and its conflict IS a syntax error — but nothing imports a selftest. It is only ever run as a script by the suite runner, so the failure is one red file in a suite, not a cascade. And if the suite runner is what is broken, or if nobody reads which file went red, it looks like an ordinary failing test.

So the file the doc gate was written to protect (CLAUDE.md) is clean, and the two files that actually reach a visitor are the ones that shipped broken.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS WORTH THE ENTRY: the loop's own commit messages are on the markers — `>>>>>>> 83d9d49 (loop: turn 90 on lp-ef6599 — awaiting verdict)` and `ff7d2d9 (loop: turn 87 on lp-3f5f26)`. Turns 87 and 90 both edited the intro region, the merge kept both sides, and at least two subsequent turns worked in this tree, read this file, and did not notice. I nearly did not either — my first Read of lines 82-105 showed `<h2 id="gameIntroTitle">` at line 95 AND at line 100 and I read straight past it.

FIXED: both index.html regions, which are in this ticket's bounded paths. Both were COMMENT-ONLY differences with byte-identical code after them (plus one style attribute), so resolution was mechanical — I took one side wholesale rather than merging prose, and recorded that as a decision. NOT FIXED: index-campaign-wiring.selftest.mjs, which is outside the bounded paths. It still cannot parse. Proposed at P0.

learned.title: An empty factory certifies ok:true — the vacuous-satisfiability trap arriving from a THIRD direction, and this one is reachable on the first frame
learned.body:
The ledger records this trap twice: dropping a refused SINK leaves a network with no sinks, which production.mjs documents as vacuously satisfiable at margin 0, so `network.ok` goes TRUE on a level that just failed; and a pocket-illegal object opens the same door. Both need the player to have done something wrong.

This one needs the player to have done NOTHING.

    pocketLevelVerdict(pocket, [], []).ok === true

`placement.every(r => r.ok)` is vacuously true of an empty array. `networkFrom` yields no nodes and no edges. `feasible` finds no sinks, so `deficits` is empty, `ok` is true and `margin` is 0. So the FULL certificate — not just its network half, which is the part the ledger warns about — reports `ok: true` before the player has touched anything.

That is not a defect in pocketLevel.mjs. It is the honest answer to 'is everything placed legal and everything demanded supplied', and for an empty factory the answer is yes. It is a defect in anything that renders it, and `ok` is exactly the field a renderer reaches for.

So `won = complete && ok`, where `complete` is 'every objective slot holds a placed object' — a property of the PALETTE, not of the certificate, which is why no amount of work inside pocketLevel.mjs could have supplied it. §1 of the new gate asserts `ok === true`, `margin === 0`, `complete === false` and `won === false` on the same empty verdict, in that order. Asserting only `won === false` would pass for an implementation that reached it by accident; asserting the four together is what makes an implementation that returns `won = v.ok` fail on the first frame rather than on some fixture nobody thought of.

GENERAL SHAPE, and it is now three instances in this file family: a certificate that quantifies over a set is TRUE of the empty set, and 'nothing has happened yet' is the most common state any UI is ever in. Any predicate of the form 'every X is fine' needs a companion asking whether there are any X at all — and the companion cannot live in the module that computes the predicate, because emptiness is a fact about the caller's intent rather than about the data.

learned.title: Two smelters share a SLOT, refused before any geometry is computed — because the alternative is feasible() throwing in front of a visitor
learned.body:
The objective declares four edges over four ids: vein→smelter, smelter→depot, vein→bigSmelter, bigSmelter→depot. If the player places BOTH smelters, the vein fans out to two processors with no explicit `share`, and production.mjs REFUSES an unsplit fan-out by throwing. A throw out of `verdict()` is a blank panel, not a refusal.

Three options considered.

  1. GIVE THE VEIN EDGES EXPLICIT SHARES. A group of two must sum to ≤ 1, so each would carry 0.5 — and a group of ONE edge with share 0.5 is also legal, meaning half the ore vanishes even when only one smelter is built. The player would be quietly penalised for a rule about a machine they did not build.
  2. CATCH THE THROW in verdict(). Turns a designed refusal into a swallowed exception, and the player learns nothing.
  3. THE SLOT RULE, taken: OBJECTIVE.slots groups ['smelter','bigSmelter'] as one slot, and `preview()` refuses a second object in a filled slot with `reason: 'slot'` BEFORE building a constellation. `verdict()` additionally filters edges to placed ids, so an edge naming an unplaced node can never reach feasible() either.

The slot check runs first and returns `con: null` deliberately, and the gate asserts that: a slot conflict is a rule of the objective, not a fact about the rock, and reporting it as a collision would point the player at entirely the wrong thing. It also makes the choice a real one with a cost — to change smelters you `remove()` the first, which is the decision the level is made of.

WHAT WOULD REVERSE IT: if a later objective genuinely wants one source feeding two processors, the fix is explicit shares in the objective literal plus dropping that key from `slots` — no change to PocketGame itself. The slot rule is data, not mechanism, which is why it was worth putting in the frozen literal rather than in the class.

learned.title: The pocket is held pristine and never planted into — so PocketGame does NOT use SummonSession, and the lattice does not visibly reform
learned.body:
The ticket named this and I want the reasoning on the record because it is the one design choice a reviewer should push on.

SummonSession really plants: its pocket advances and its seed count grows. pocketLevelVerdict takes a pocket and an ordered object list and APPENDS each legal object's seeds itself. Hand it a session's grown pocket and every placed seed is counted twice, and each object is checked against a copy of itself — which refuses everything for `step`, at gap 0. That is a wrong answer, not a crash, and it would have looked like a mysteriously unbuildable level.

So the pristine pocket is generated once and every verdict is recomputed by replaying the ordered list. Three things fall out, and two are wins:

  · `remove(id)` is a splice. An undo of a real lattice rebuild is NOT one line — summon-session.mjs's header explains that membrane open/closed state is carried by the caller, so restoring a pocket without restoring what was opened would silently reset the level.
  · `preview()` is exact rather than approximate: it replays the whole list with the proposed object appended and reads the last entry, so it accounts for everything already down.
  · THE COST: the foam does not bend around a placed machine. You see where it went, not the lattice reforming. Ask lp-2fadad is open on whether that reform IS the point of the game.

WHAT WOULD REVERSE IT: if the reform is the point, switch to a SummonSession and take the production half from level.mjs's `networkFrom` over session-local placements — which is a change inside this one file, and that is precisely why this was the reversible choice to make first.

learned.title: Two gates would have gone red for reasons that have nothing to do with this module — one caught, one avoided by reading the slicing code first
learned.body:
Eight gates read index.html as text and the last page ticket was REJECTED for breaking four it never named. So before writing anything I read how each one finds its subject:

    index-campaign-wiring  slices on explicit markers // CAMPAIGN BLOCK BEGIN/END
    index-summon-wiring    slices html.indexOf('import { SummonSession') to EOF

That pair pins where a new block may go: AFTER `// CAMPAIGN BLOCK END` and BEFORE the SummonSession import. Anywhere after that import and my code lands inside the summon gate's slice, where it would trip that gate's negative assertions (no hand-typed solid name, no re-typed placement threshold) for code that has nothing to do with the summon panel. My block is placed exactly in that window and carries its own BEGIN/END markers so it can move later without breaking its own gate.

THE ONE I CAUGHT IN MY OWN GATE, and it is the more useful half. §6 forbids any literal derived from OBJECTIVE at run time — {60, 15, 25, 20} after filtering out values ≤ 3, which are ordinary numbers in any page. My first version tested those against the WHOLE page text. The summon plan already ships `style="...height:20rem..."`, and `(?<![\w.])20(?![0-9.])` matches it: the character before is `:` and the character after is `r`. So the gate would have gone red over a stylesheet, on a page that was completely correct.

Scoped to my own block instead, with the reason written at the assertion. This is the recorded 'a checker that fails correct work is worse than no checker' shape, and note WHERE it came from: not from the module under test, and not from my own block, but from an unrelated panel three hundred lines away that happens to use a round number in a CSS unit. A whole-file negation over numeric literals is almost always too wide, because the page is shared and the numbers are not.

Also checked and clear: no id matching /id="lvl\d*"/ (index-campaign-wiring §7 asserts zero), no `feasible(` anywhere in the page, no `drawLevel(` added (its count must stay exactly 1), no LEVEL_1 reference, and no duplicate top-level binding — the whole <script> is ONE module and the summon block already binds `hullBounds`, `planShapes` and `PLAN`, so mine are imported under aliases. A duplicate declaration there would have been a syntax error killing the entire page, which is the same failure I had just spent the turn fixing.

learned.title: The placed machines render as `mine` through planShapes with no new drawing code — a display pocket, not a second renderer
learned.body:
The panel needs to draw the pristine pocket's seeds AND everything the player has placed, visually distinguished. planShapes already draws exactly that distinction: it takes `originCount` and marks every seed at or past it as `mine`, because in a SummonSession those are the ones the player planted.

Since this module keeps the pocket pristine, its `pocket.seeds` never grows — so passing it directly would draw the rock and none of the machines. The fix is one line and no new rule:

    { ...pg.pocket, seeds: [...pg.pocket.seeds, ...st.placed.flatMap(p => p.seeds)] }

with `originCount = pg.pocket.seeds.length`. The composed list is exactly the seed list a session WOULD have had, in exactly the order pocketPlacementReport accumulates them, so `mine` means the same thing it has always meant and the summon panel's own colours apply unchanged.

Worth recording because the tempting alternative is a `kind: 'placed'` descriptor and a branch in the renderer — a second way of saying 'the player put this here', free to drift from the first. The general shape: when a renderer already distinguishes A from B by a BOUNDARY INDEX rather than by a flag on each item, you can feed it a synthetic list and get the distinction for free, provided you can honestly reproduce the ordering. Here the ordering is guaranteed because it is the same accumulation the verdict uses.

learned.title: Nothing was executed, and the region I would read first is §4 — because I wrote it badly twice
learned.body:
No Bash. The standing recommendation about gate-bearing turns is in this ledger well past twenty-five times and recent turns agreed to stop restating it; I am not restating it. What is worth an entry is that this turn's residual risk is NOT the usual arithmetic one, and I know exactly where it is.

THE NUMBERS ARE THE SAFE PART. Every production value is integer arithmetic chosen so hand-verification is exact rather than approximate: ore 60, input 3 per gear, so the supply-bound scale is 60/3 = 20 for both smelters. Small capacity 15 binds below 20 and makes 15 gear against a demand of 20 — short by exactly 5. Big capacity 25 does not bind, so it makes exactly 20 and the margin is exactly 0. No division that does not terminate, no float comparison anywhere in the asserted values.

THE UNSAFE PART IS §4, THE ROLLBACK BLOCK, and it is unsafe because of how I wrote it rather than because of what it claims. My first draft left two assertions ending in `|| true` — placeholders from a half-finished edit, which is to say assertions that CANNOT FAIL. That is the single worst defect an unrun gate can carry: a wrong literal is loud, a vacuous assertion is silent forever, and this file's whole subject is a claim that nothing changed. My second draft was worse in a different way — it referenced a name I had not declared, which would have thrown at run time. The third is plain: snapshot with `moves` normalised out on both sides, compare for exact equality, assert the move count separately, and keep the serializer control that proves the comparator can see a difference at all.

I am recording it rather than quietly fixing it because the failure mode is instructive. Both bad drafts came from trying to write the assertion and the normalisation in one expression while I could not run it to see the shape. With no execution, the pressure is to write the clever compact form because you cannot iterate — and the clever compact form is exactly where a vacuous assertion hides. The discipline that worked was: name the normalisation, name the snapshot, then compare two names.

SECOND RESIDUAL, smaller: §0 asserts the sweep finds four mutually clear centres at least 22 m apart in this pocket. That is a claim about the FIXTURE, not the module, and it is the one assertion that would go red if generatePocket's output ever moved. It fails with its own message and exits before anything else runs, so a fixture failure cannot be mistaken for a module failure.

propose.title: Repair the three merge conflicts in plant/test/index-campaign-wiring.selftest.mjs — the file cannot parse, so the suite cannot pass and deploy-plant cannot publish
propose.body:
plant/test/index-campaign-wiring.selftest.mjs carries THREE unresolved conflict regions, one of them NESTED:

    48   <<<<<<< HEAD
    49   <<<<<<< HEAD        <- nested inside the first
    56   =======
    57   >>>>>>> 83d9d49 (loop: turn 90 on lp-ef6599)
    59   =======
    61   >>>>>>> ff7d2d9 (loop: turn 87 on lp-3f5f26)
    252  <<<<<<< HEAD
    318  =======
    378  >>>>>>> 83d9d49 (loop: turn 90 on lp-ef6599)

A conflict marker in a .mjs file is a syntax error, so this gate does not run AT ALL — it does not fail an assertion, it fails to parse. Consequences, in order of cost:

  1. deploy-plant runs the whole plant/ suite BEFORE wrangler is invoked, so nothing in plant/ can be published until this is repaired. Every turn's visible output is blocked behind it.
  2. The page assertions this gate owns — that the campaign block re-types no level literal, that the six scrolled sections are gone, that INTRO and LINES are rendered by reference — are currently unchecked. Any regression in them since turn 87 would have gone unnoticed.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE DELETE. The 252-378 region is a 126-line span covering whole sections (8) and (9x); the two sides are different generations of the intro-ownership assertions from lp-ef6599 and lp-3f5f26. Whoever takes it must decide which section set is current against the index.html that exists TODAY — and index.html changed in this same turn (its own two conflicts resolved, plus an additive panel). So the repair is: resolve, then read the surviving assertions against the current page, then run it.

The nested region at 48-61 is imports and is likely mechanical; the large one is not.

SCOPE: plant/test/index-campaign-wiring.selftest.mjs only. GATE: the file itself must run and pass.

I could not do this: the file is outside this ticket's bounded paths and a diff outside them discards the whole turn.

propose.title: docs.selftest.mjs walks only .md — extend the conflict-marker check to .mjs, .js and .html under plant/, which is where the markers that actually shipped were
propose.body:
test/docs.selftest.mjs exists because a merge conflict shipped in plant/CLAUDE.md and nothing went red. Its header argues, correctly, that a marker in a .mjs file is a syntax error that fails loudly while in markdown it is inert — and on that basis it walks ONLY `.md`.

THAT ARGUMENT HAS TWO HOLES AND BOTH WERE OCCUPIED THIS TURN.

  · AN HTML FILE IS NOT PARSED BY ANY GATE. Eight selftests read plant/index.html with readFileSync and run regexes over it. Text does not parse, so index.html sat with a conflict INSIDE its <script type="module"> — a dead page on plant.minomobi.com — while every one of those gates passed. The duplicated content even satisfies presence checks twice over.
  · A SELFTEST IS NEVER IMPORTED. plant/test/index-campaign-wiring.selftest.mjs is a .mjs whose conflict IS a syntax error, but nothing imports a selftest — it is run as a script, so the 'loud' failure is one red file among thirty, which reads like an ordinary failing assertion rather than like a broken merge.

So the file the check protects was clean and the two files that reach a visitor were not.

WHAT TO BUILD: extend the walk to `.md`, `.mjs`, `.js` and `.html` under plant/. The marker predicate and the fenced-code exemption are already written and already have their controls — including the recorded subtlety that a bare whole-line `=======` is only a conflict when an unclosed `<<<<<<< ` sits above it, because a setext heading underline is exactly a line of equals signs.

TWO THINGS THE NEW FILE TYPES NEED THAT MARKDOWN DID NOT:
  · the fence exemption is a MARKDOWN rule. In .mjs and .html it must not apply, or a marker inside a template literal containing backticks is exempted for no reason. Simplest correct split: fenced-code exemption for .md only, unconditional scan for the rest.
  · docs.selftest.mjs must not scan ITSELF into a false positive — it necessarily contains marker literals. The existing file already builds them with `'<'.repeat(7)` precisely so no line of it begins with a marker, and the recorded reasoning for that is worth preserving: a hand-typed run of seven identical characters is the one defect a suite of self-consistent fixtures cannot detect, because the fixtures and the predicate are wrong together.

CONTROLS THE GATE MUST CARRY, or it proves nothing: a synthetic .html fixture with a marker must FIRE; a synthetic .mjs with a marker must FIRE; the real tree must be clean; and the walk must be asserted non-empty and to have found files of each new extension by name — the realistic way this silently stops working is a walk that comes back empty and passes every negation.

This is the systemic fix for the dead-end filed alongside. The bead above is the specific one.

propose.title: Give the pocket game a second objective, and take the objective from a list the way campaign.mjs takes levels
propose.body:
pocket-game.mjs ships ONE frozen OBJECTIVE and PocketGame already takes it as a constructor argument (`new PocketGame({ objective })`), so the mechanism for a second one exists and is untested by anything but the default.

WHY A SECOND ONE IS WORTH A TURN AND A SEVENTH LEVEL WAS NOT. The vision is explicit that another network literal with different numbers is tiling rather than a curve. This is not that: the pocket game's difficulty axis is GEOMETRIC — how much clear ground the objective needs relative to how much the pocket has — and that axis has exactly one sample today. A second objective that is tight in SPACE rather than in RATE would establish whether the two failure modes can be traded against each other, which is the thing this panel exists to find out and currently cannot answer.

CONCRETE SHAPE: a second objective on a DIFFERENT pocket seed, needing four machines rather than three, where the big smelter's larger footprint means the rate-sufficient choice is the one that may not fit. That makes the choice genuinely two-sided — the small smelter loses on rate, the big one may lose on room — instead of the current 'the big one is simply better if you can afford the space'.

WHAT THE GATE MUST ADD, beyond re-running the existing sections against the new literal:
  · a scripted playthrough of objective 2 that wins in a bounded number of moves, with the bound asserted;
  · the DISCRIMINATING pair: a centre at which the big smelter is refused for geometry and the small one is legal, in the same pocket, asserted as two verdicts differing in one field. Without that pair the second objective is only a third set of numbers.
  · an assertion that the two objectives' win bounds DIFFER, so 'harder' is a measured claim rather than a label.

Deliberately NOT proposed: a computed difficulty ORDER over objectives, à la campaign.mjs's winFraction. Win fraction is a property of a finite declared domain, and this game's domain is continuous (any point on the plan), so the measure does not transfer and inventing one is its own ticket.

propose.title: Highlight where the selected machine WOULD fit — but not from the front of candidates(), which is one column at n heights
propose.body:
The pocket panel currently gives no positive guidance: a stranger clicks, is refused, and has to hunt. The summon panel solves this with green candidate dots, and the obvious move is to do the same here.

THE TICKET FOR THIS PANEL EXPLICITLY FORBADE DOING IT THIS TURN, and the recorded reason is worth restating because it is the exact trap: SummonSession.candidates() sweeps `for x { for z { for ys } }` and pushes in that order, so `list.slice(0, n)` is ONE (x, z) COLUMN at n different heights — not n places, one place at n altitudes. A highlight built from the front of that list would read as 'you may only build here', pointing at a single spot, which is worse than no guidance because it is confidently wrong.

WHAT TO BUILD INSTEAD: a sweep that takes an index STRIDE across the whole candidate list rather than a prefix, at the fixed height the panel places at, filtered through PocketGame.preview() so the highlight accounts for machines already placed — which candidates() cannot do, since it knows nothing about this game's ordered list.

WHAT THE GATE MUST ASSERT, and the third one is the one that bites:
  · every highlighted point previews ok:true — a highlight that lies is the whole failure mode;
  · the highlight SHRINKS after a machine is placed near it, proving it accounts for the accumulated list rather than the static pocket;
  · CONDITIONALLY, the highlighted points cover more than one (x, z) column — written as 'IF the sweep found more than one column, the highlight covers more than one'. Unconditionally is wrong: a pocket tight enough that every legal centre sits in one column is a legitimate fixture, and asserting the strong form would fail a gate about highlighting for a reason that has nothing to do with highlighting. The temptation to assert the strong form is strongest exactly when you have just been burned by the weak one.

Also worth pinning: the highlight must be recomputed on `remove()` as well as on `place()`, which is the case a cache gets wrong.

asks.title: Is a three-move win with one real decision a level, or a demonstration?
asks.body:
The objective is: put a vein, a smelter and a depot into the rock and the depot is fed. A blind player who picks three clear spots and takes the big smelter wins in three moves. The only genuine decision is which smelter — and once you have read that one makes 15 gear and the other 20 against a demand of 20, it is not much of a decision.

I cannot settle this from here and it is not a matter of writing a better check. Every gateable property is already gated: the bound is asserted, the two failure modes are asserted distinguishable in one verdict, the refusal a player causes is reachable in two moves. What none of that measures is whether the thing is INTERESTING, and the vision's bar — 'an intention they formed, acted on, and got refused for' — is met by the letter (you will be refused if you put the depot on the vein) while possibly missing the spirit (nobody FORMS the intention to stack two machines; they do it by accident).

The honest worry is that the geometry and the production halves do not yet TRADE against each other. Space is abundant in this pocket, so the spatial half is a formality and the rate half is a one-bit choice. A level where the rate-sufficient machine is the one that might not fit is the version where both halves matter at once — I have proposed it, but whether it is the right next move depends on how this one actually plays.
asks.do: Open plant.minomobi.com (AFTER the two P0 gate repairs land — the page is currently dead and the panel will not publish until the suite passes). Scroll to 'Feed the depot'. Play it once without reading the module. Then deliberately try to stack two machines on the same spot, and try to put one through a wall.
asks.watch: Whether you ever have to CHOOSE between putting a machine somewhere convenient and somewhere legal — or whether there is so much room that position never costs you anything. And whether the small-smelter failure reads as your mistake or as the level withholding a number you could not have known.
asks.soThat: If position never costs anything, the next objective is the tight-space one I proposed (P2) and it should go to P0 — the geometry half is currently decorative. If the small-smelter failure reads as withheld information, the fix is showing each machine's rate on its palette button, which is a small page ticket. If it plays as a level already, then the pocket game is item 1 delivered and the next turns belong on the second objective rather than on this one.
